judge: listening-judge (two independent model passes, keys withheld, per-pass per-row option shuffle)
note: Two independent blind passes over the authored N5 sokuji-outou candidates; the 5 burned rows were replaced by newly authored rows judged in their own packets under the same protocol. Packets were shuffled INDEPENDENTLY per row per pass, so the key never sat in the same option slot twice and position could not leak the answer. A row ships only when BOTH passes return PASS and both picks are the frozen key. AMBIGUOUS means two of the four responses are what a native speaker would actually give, which is the defect a 聴解 store cannot carry: the heard scenario must decide ONE answer.

why: pass1 AMBIGUOUS: A (yes, a little) and C (no, I'm still studying) are both defensible answers to the same question.
pass1 AMBIGUOUS: C (yes, please) grants and B (no, already opened) is a defensible reason-based refusal; both respond to the same permission request.
pass1 AMBIGUOUS: A (thanks, I'll dig in) accepts and D (no, I already ate) is a natural decline of the same food offer.
pass2 AMBIGUOUS: An offer of food accepts ("ありがとうございます、いただきます") and politely declines with a reason ("いいえ、もう たべました") equally well; two options are defensible.
pass2 AMBIGUOUS: The refusal "いいえ、けっこうです、だいじょうぶです" and the accepting "ええ、とても おもいです" (yes, it is heavy) are both responses a native would give to this offer of help.
pass1 AMBIGUOUS: A (yes, really fun) agrees but C (no, I haven't seen it yet) is a natural correction of the shared-experience presupposition.
pass2 AMBIGUOUS: Agreeing ("ええ、ほんとうに たのしかったです") and correcting the premise ("いいえ、まだ みて いません", I haven't seen it yet) are both natural replies to this ですね remark.
